principles.description: Ordinary interactive surfaces move into their existing depth on hover and press; generic upward hover lift is prohibited.
Interaction feedback must make cause, state, and result legible instead of adding decorative motion without meaning.
Motion may reinforce a state change, but text and programmatic state remain authoritative when motion is absent.
Reduced-motion and forced-colors behavior are product requirements, not optional presentation fallbacks.

patterns.title: Tactile press
patterns.description: Raised controls compress into their shadow. Fine-pointer hover consumes part of the depth; active consumes the remaining shadow without moving the pointer hit target away during activation.

evidence.marker: reduced-motion mode removes smooth scrolling and tactile animation

patterns.title: Latched selection
patterns.description: A selected option remains visibly and programmatically latched instead of appearing to float. Product media demonstrates pointer and arrow-key selection with one active tab.

patterns.title: Processing feedback
patterns.description: Loading motion may reinforce processing, but it never replaces explicit status. The skeleton animation becomes static when reduced motion is requested.

patterns.title: Result feedback
patterns.description: Commerce mutations expose a persistent textual and programmatic result. Motion is optional reinforcement; lifecycle state remains legible without animation.

exceptions.description: Semantic lift is permitted only while an object is actually picked up for dragging. Hover alone never lifts an ordinary control.

evidence.marker: Semantic lift is reserved for actions such as actually dragging an object.
